fields.summary: Unify Policy Creation UI across Metric, APM, RUM, NetRoute with single “Set Conditions” experience (Threshold + Baseline + Anomaly + Forecast)

issuetype.name: Story

fields.description:
h2. Problem Statement

Today, *Anomaly* and *Forecast* policies are configured via separate flows, which creates {*}UX confusion{*}, {*}feature discoverability issues{*}, and {*}higher support cost{*}. Additionally, *APM/RUM/NetRoute* do not support {*}Baseline Alert{*}, creating a functional mismatch vs Metric policies.

 
h2. Goal

Deliver a *single, consistent Create Policy experience* (as per new UI screenshots) where users configure:
 * *Threshold Alert*

 * *Baseline Alert*

 * *Anomaly*

 * {*}Forecast{*}{*}{*}

*from the* *same screen* *for* {*}Metric, APM, RUM, NetRoute{*}{*}{*}
h2. User Story

As a {*}platform user configuring alert policies{*}, I want a *single unified policy creation flow* for Metric/APM/RUM/NetRoute so that I can configure Threshold/Baseline/Anomaly/Forecast {*}without switching to separate policy modules{*}, and I get a predictable policy setup pattern across modules.
h2. Scope
h3. In Scope
 # *Unified Create Policy UI* for these modules:

 ** Metric

 ** APM

 ** RUM

 ** NetRoute

 # “Set Conditions” section supports these modes {*}as tabs{*}:

 ** Threshold Alert

 ** Baseline Alert

 ** Anomaly

 ** Forecast

 # *Baseline Alert support added for APM, RUM, NetRoute*

 # Module-specific fields retained, but aligned layout:

 ** Metric: Counter, Source Filter, Source

 # Existing downstream sections remain consistent:

 ** Set Alert Message

 ** Notify Team

 ** Take Action

 ** Declare Incident

h2. UX Requirements
h3. Step 1

User navigates: *Policies → Create Policy → selects module (Metric/APM/RUM/NetRoute)*
h3. Step 2

User enters:
 * Policy Name (required)

 * Tag (required/optional based on current standard)

h3. Step 3 — Set Conditions

User selects one of:
 * Threshold Alert

 * Baseline Alert

 * Anomaly

 * Forecast

h3. Step 4 — Configure fields 

User selects Counter, Source Filter, Source and sets severity thresholds/baseline/anomaly/forecast parameters.
h3. Step 5 — Configure notification and actions

User expands remaining accordions:
 * Alert message

 * Notify team

 * Take action

 * Declare incident

h3. Step 6 — Save

User clicks *Create Policy*
System validates + persists config + shows success.
h2. Acceptance Criteria
h3. A. Unified Navigation & Layout
 # For {*}Metric, APM, RUM, NetRoute{*}, the Create Policy screen uses the {*}same layout structure{*}: header + basic fields + Set Conditions + remaining accordions.

 # “Set Conditions” contains *four tabs* in the same order:

 ** Threshold Alert | Baseline Alert | Anomaly | Forecast

 # *Anomaly* and *Forecast* are no longer separate standalone policy creation flows

*B. Field Behaviour & Validation*
 # *Policy Name* is mandatory; Create Policy is disabled until provided.

 # *Counter* is mandatory for all four tabs 

 # *Source Filter* and *Source* behaviour is consistent:

 ** Source Filter selection controls Source list.

 ** Source is required when Source Filter is not “Everywhere/All”.

 # Severity inputs behave consistently:

 ** Critical / Major / Warning are available as per your UI standard.

 ** Operator dropdown works (Equals/Greater than/Less than etc.) and persists.

 # “Notify if breach within” / “Abnormality Occurrence” / “Auto Clear” are available and persist as per selected policy tab (threshold/baseline/anomaly/forecast-specific rules must be enforced).

h3. D. Module-Specific Rules
 # APM policy supports its module-specific *Policy Type* switch (e.g., Trace Metrics / Trace Analytics) and it correctly filters available counters.

 # RUM policy shows only RUM-eligible counters and source filters.

 # NetRoute policy shows only NetRoute-eligible counters and source filters.

 # Metric policy retains current capabilities and does not lose existing counters or sources.

h3. F. Migration & Backward Compatibility
 # Existing Threshold policies for all modules remain functional with {*}no behavioral change{*}.

 # Existing Anomaly/Forecast policies (if any exist today) continue to function

h2. Use Cases & Test Scenarios:
h3. Use Case 1 — Metric Threshold policy
 * Create Metric policy → Threshold Alert

 * Select Counter = CPU Utilization

 * Source Filter = Group, Source = “Linux Servers”

 * Set Critical > 85, Major > 75, Warning > 60

 * Save → verify in list → simulate breach → alert generated

h3. Use Case 2 — APM Baseline policy
 * Create APM policy → Policy Type = Trace Metrics

 * Baseline Alert tab

 * Select Counter = Avg Response Time

 * Source Filter = Service, Source = “Checkout Service”

 * Save → verify baseline deviations raise alerts (or confirm baseline evaluation window behavior)

h3. Use Case 3 — RUM Anomaly policy 
 * Create RUM policy → Anomaly tab

 * Counter = Page Load Time (or relevant)

 * Source Filter = Application, Source = “Customer Portal”

 * Configure occurrence threshold

 * Save → ensure anomaly policy is created without leaving the Create Policy flow

h3. Use Case 4 — NetRoute Forecast policy 
 * Create NetRoute policy → Forecast tab

 * Counter = Link Utilization

 * Source Filter = Interface, Source = “WAN Interface”

 * Configure forecast horizon / threshold

 * Save → verify forecast alert generation logic is wired

h3. Use Case 6 — Edit existing policy
 * Open an existing Threshold policy (APM/RUM/NetRoute)

 * UI must render correctly in the unified screen

 * Update threshold values → Save → verify updated values persist and execute

## Manual QA Test Plan — MOTADATA-8503

- [ ] Create Metric Threshold via the new tabbed UI. Route: Settings -> Policy -> Metric Policy -> + Create Policy. Verify the four-card tab strip renders, Threshold is selected by default, only the active card has the primary border. Fill required fields, save, expect 'Policy created successfully' toast and a new row in the list. Console must be clean.
- [ ] Edit any existing Metric policy. Verify the four tab cards render with cursor:not-allowed, opacity ~0.6, and clicking a different tab does NOTHING. No console errors.
- [ ] Create a Baseline Alert from the new tab. Verify baselineAlertValueType defaults to 'Relative'. Save and re-open the policy - confirm the value persists.
- [ ] Create an Anomaly Alert. Verify the Anomaly conditions render (sample lookup field appears). Save and confirm the list row's policyTypeDisplay is human-readable (not '[object Object]', not blank).
- [ ] Create a Forecast Alert (Metric). Verify the severity selection works, the forecast threshold field validates as required, and the saved policy appears with policyTypeDisplay 'Metric Forecast' (or whatever the server returns).
- [ ] License gating: log in as a user WITHOUT FORECAST_LICENSE_PERMISSION. Verify only three tabs render. Repeat without ANOMALY_LICENSE_PERMISSION - only Threshold + Baseline should render.
- [ ] Open an EXISTING Forecast policy as a user without the Forecast license (simulate license downgrade). Verify the UI doesn't crash and the user has a clear signal that this subtype is no longer available.
- [ ] Navigate to Settings -> Policy -> APM Policy. Verify the 'Apm Policy Type' column shows the full server-side string for every row (e.g. 'Trace Metrics', 'APM Metric Anomaly', 'APM Metric Baseline', 'APM Metric Forecast'), not the collapsed bucket value.
- [ ] Filter the APM Policy list by typing 'Forecast' into the policy-type column search box. Verify rows actually filter (Network tab: no 4xx; result count changes). If filter is server-side and returns 0 results, this is the column-key regression flagged in the review.
- [ ] Create an APM Trace Metrics policy for each subtype (Threshold, Anomaly, Baseline, Forecast). For each: save, confirm row appears with correct policyTypeDisplay, edit it, confirm subtype tabs are disabled in edit mode.
- [ ] Create a RUM Metric policy for each subtype. Special check: for RUM Baseline and RUM Anomaly, try saving WITHOUT entering any severity value. The form must block submit with a clear validation message - if it accepts and saves an empty policy, the RUM Baseline/Anomaly validation gap (flagged Major) has shipped.
- [ ] Open a RUM Metric Forecast policy in view mode (is-view=true). Verify all fields render read-only. The Forecast subtype tab is highlighted but not clickable.
- [ ] Trigger or pick an APM Metric Forecast alert. Navigate to Alerts -> All Alerts -> click the row. Verify: (a) Alert Type cell shows the full APM policy type. (b) History timeline entries do NOT contain the literal text 'undefined' anywhere. (c) The trend chart renders as a forecast widget (DevTools Network: request body category 'forecast'). (d) Service name is non-blank.
- [ ] Trigger an APM Metric Anomaly alert. Open the detail page. Verify the trend chart renders WITH data (no 'No data' placeholder). This catches the silent regression of the 9ae048a25 widget-context fix.
- [ ] Trigger an APM Metric Baseline alert. Same check as the Anomaly case.
- [ ] Trigger a RUM Metric Forecast alert. Verify the trend chart renders as a PLAIN line chart, not a forecast widget (RUM forecast is intentionally excluded by isRumMetricForecast).
- [ ] Forecast history-text edge cases: confirm that 'Auto Clear' clear-state entries read 'has enter into clear state, with value Auto Clear'. Non-clear entries read '...is trending towards a <severity> state, expected to surpass <threshold>% within <time>.' Verify NO 'undefined' tokens appear in either path.
- [ ] Light vs dark theme on the new tab UI. Inspect a policy-tab-item card in light theme: active background should be visibly tinted with the primary color. Toggle to dark theme. Verify the inactive tab background is NOT transparent/black - this is the --bg-neutral-lightest non-existent-token regression.
- [ ] Run npm run lint:stylelint -- 'src/design/policy-tab.less' AND any updated conditions templates. The double-underscore/double-hyphen class names will fail the pre-commit hook - this MUST be fixed before merge.
- [ ] Run npm run lint and npm run test:unit on the branch. Confirm both pass.
- [ ] Non-touched policy types (Log, Flow, Trap, NetRoute, Availability): create one of each via the existing flow. Confirm the new tab strip does NOT appear and the existing behaviour is unchanged.

*Verified* threshold, baseline (absolute + relative), anomaly, forecast for RUM policies — all working as expected. Marking this task as {*}done{*}.

*Note:* Anomaly alerts could not be triggered for RUM events as the RUM event data cannot be manipulated for testing purposes.
Verified threshold, baseline (absolute + relative), anomaly, forecast for APM policies — all working as expected. Marking this task as done.
